title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from pages 76 and 78. A 'spatios' (Grothendieck's coined term, read here as such) is a structure (Σ, ≤, C): a complete ordered set with a complementation C. Judging from how it is used, it behaves like a complete ortholattice. A 'disposition' on a set E is a symmetric relation x|o|y ('x and y are disjoint/orthogonal'). In modern language this is an orthogonality space in the sense of Dacey, Foulis and Randall.

From (E,|o|) Grothendieck forms Σ_E, the set of subsets A ⊂ E that are closed for the polarity A ↦ Comp^o(A) = {x : x|o|a for all a ∈ A}, i.e. A = A^{oo}. Σ_E is ordered by inclusion and has complementation Comp^o. There is a canonical map σ_E : E → Σ_E, presumably x ↦ {x}^{oo}.

Any spatios gives a disposition: x|o|y iff x ≤ Cy. Proposition 1 (p.76) says that then σ : Σ → Σ_Σ is an isomorphism, with inverse S ↦ sup S. The Scholie identifies spatios structures on a set with the dispositions for which σ is bijective.

This page opens: 'Ainsi, les spatios peuvent être considérés comme des dispositions particulières, qu'on pourrait appeler les dispositions canoniques.' For an arbitrary disposition E, Grothendieck wants (Σ_E, σ_E) to be 'the' canonical disposition, i.e. the spatios associated with E. He wants it characterized up to unique isomorphism.

Proposition 2. Let (E,|o|) be a disposition, Σ a spatios, and σ : E → Σ a map. There is an isomorphism α : Σ_E ≅ Σ with α∘σ_E = σ iff two conditions hold:
(a) for all x, y: x|o|y ⇔ σx |o| σy, i.e. σx ≤ Cσy. So σ preserves and reflects orthogonality.
(b) (p.78) every S ∈ Σ satisfies S = sup{σx : σx ≤ S}. So σ(E) is join-dense.
The isomorphism is then unique.

Proof (p.78). Put α(A) = sup σ(A). This is monotone, and surjective by (b). Set β(S) = {x : σx ≤ S}. Using (a) and the fact that σx ⊥ T ⇔ σx ⊥ sup T, one shows β(S) = Comp^o(β(CS)), so β(S) ∈ Σ_E, and β is inverse to α.

This is the abstract characterization of the 'completion' of an orthogonality space, analogous to the characterization of the Dedekind–MacNeille completion by density of the embedding.
errors: Notation slip. The statement names the map E → Σ 'α', but the diagram labels the top arrow σ and the vertical isomorphism α (with ≀). The conditions and the proof on p.78 use σ for E → Σ and α for Σ_E → Σ. So the statement's 'α : E → Σ' should read σ, and the 'φ' in the transcription is the iso α.
Condition (a) is left unfinished on this page (the right-hand side 'αx|o|αy' is crossed out); it is completed in substance on p.78 as σx|o|σy.

Implicit hypotheses: Σ must be complete, and the complementation must satisfy x ≤ Cy ⇔ y ≤ Cx and σx ⊥ sup T ⇔ σx ⊥ t for all t ∈ T (ortholattice-type axioms). The proof relies on these silently. No mathematical error otherwise.

ideas.what: Spatios (complete ordered set with complementation) viewed as a special 'canonical' disposition (orthogonality relation x ⊥ y iff x ≤ Cy)
ideas.modern_name: Complete ortholattice as an orthogonality space; Galois polarity of orthogonality

ideas.what: Σ_E = ortho-closed subsets (A = A^{oo}) of a disposition E with σ_E : E → Σ_E, characterized up to unique iso by orthogonality-reflecting + join-dense maps (Proposition 2)
ideas.modern_name: Universal/density characterization of the ortholattice of an orthogonality space (MacNeille-type completion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacNeille (1937) for the order case; Dacey, Foulis–Randall, Moore and others for orthogonality spaces

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct but classical lattice-theoretic result: the ortholattice of closed sets of an orthogonality space, characterized by a join-dense orthogonality-reflecting map. It is interesting only biographically, as Grothendieck redeveloping orthogonality spaces under his own terminology ('dispositions', 'spatios') in 1986. Nothing new for specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'disjonction(s)' should read 'disposition(s)', consistent with 'structure de disposition' on p.76: 'les spatios peuvent être considérés comme des dispositions particulières qu'on pourrait appeler les dispositions canoniques'.
'opération(s)' should read 'spatios', the same coined term as on p.76: '(ou spatios) associé à E', 'le spatios Σ_E'.
In the diagram, the top arrow E → Σ is labelled σ (an earlier label is crossed out), and the vertical arrow between Σ and Σ_E is labelled 'α' with ≀, not φ.
Line 'Je viens déjà de construire' reads approximately: 'J'en ai déjà construit ... i.e. un[?] ... : le spatios Σ_E et l'application σ'.
'il faut et il suffit que σ satisfasse aux conditions suivantes' is correct as written (σ, not α); 'les' is crossed out and replaced by 'aux'.
Condition a): '∀x,y ∈ E, x|o|y ⇔' followed by a crossed-out 'σx|o|σy' (not αx|o|αy).
